## Apptivo at a glance

![Apptivo review ](https://www.method.me/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/Apptivo.jpg)

Apptivo launched in 2009, and today, more than 150,000 businesses use it for CRM software, project management, invoicing, and day-to-day communication.

Apptivo’s pricing is structured per user, paid monthly, and can be billed annually. Every paid plan comes with core CRM functions, mobile app access (iOS and Android), and 24/7 customer support. According to its pricing packages, you get an all-in-one CRM starting with the Premium plan. As with any other tool, the higher the tier, the more features are offered.

You can choose the free plan with limited features, featuring basic CRM apps and templates, or go with the free trial of the Ultimate plan to try out the full user experience before fully committing.

### **Apptivo pricing** 💰

Here are the pricing tiers for Apptivo:

- **Standard:** Free forever

Includes access for up to 3 users, core CRM features (contacts, customers, leads, opportunities), basic project and invoicing tools, email templates, document storage (500 MB), and community support.

- **Lite**: $15 per user/month (annual billing)

Includes 18 apps, 100 custom fields per app, 25 workflows, 8 custom dashboards, mobile app access, basic automation (e.g., lead and contact management, deal and opportunity management), third-party integrations, and 24/7 support.

- **Premium**: $25 per user/month (annual billing)

Includes 46 apps, 250 custom fields, 75 workflows, 25 dashboards, mobile app access, more automation features (e.g., relationships, e-commerce, marketing), third-party integrations, and 24/7 support.

- **Ultimate**: $40 per user/month (annual billing)

Includes 57 apps, 350 custom fields, 150 workflows, 50 dashboards, advanced automation, mobile app access, third-party integrations, and 24/7 support.

- **Enterprise**: Custom pricing

Includes 65 apps, 500 custom fields, 300 workflows, 100 dashboards, complete automations, custom integrations, Service Level Agreement (SLA)-backed support, and an account manager.

### **Apptivo core modules** 💻

Apptivo’s modular design means you only pick what fits your setup. Here’s what the platform’s big four modules offer:

- **CRM software:** If you’re still [relying on Excel](https://www.method.me/blog/stop-using-excel-as-a-crm/), updating data is likely a struggle. Apptivo’s CRM system ensures every change is tracked, with built-in lead and contact management, sales pipeline tracking, dashboards, and custom fields per app, so you tailor the system to match how your team operates.

- **Project management:** Assign tasks, track progress, link to customer data, and keep projects aligned with finances and contacts.
- **Invoicing:** Handle quotes, billing, payment tracking, and even expense reporting right in the same system. Ties into your CRM data for smoother workflows.
- **Help Desk:** Manage support cases, tickets, and communication directly through the platform. This way, customer issues live in the same system as your CRM and finance workflows. No need for unnecessary back-and-forth.

With these modules, it’s no surprise that businesses trust Apptivo. But no two businesses run the same way, and what works for one, may not be the best fit for another. Some of Apptivo’s potential challenges may be a deal-breaker for some businesses (including you), and that’s worth thinking about before making the switch.

## Where Apptivo falls short ❌

Let’s now discuss the drawbacks to using Apptivo. These are worth knowing as, depending on your needs, they can slow down your team, limit how well the system fits your workflow, and add on extra costs you didn’t prepare for.

### **User interface and menu clutter**

Some users have reported that Apptivo has a user interface (UI) thatcan look and feel dated, and that time can be wasted clicking around to find basic actions like logging a call or updating a task.

UI inconsistencies include clipped text and extra clicks to view details that make navigation frustrating and inefficient for power users.

![](https://www.method.me/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/image-3.png)

If you’re used to sleek, user-friendly software, Apptivo might disappoint. Clutter adds extra steps to simple jobs, which can slow down your team and make onboarding harder for new users.

### **Limited marketplace integrations**

Apptivo offers integrations with go-to business tools like Google Workspace (including Gmail), Microsoft Outlook, Dropbox, and Stripe. It lets you connect with over 65 business applications, but that’s still fewer than competitors that pack in far more options. Apptivo also doesn’t sync natively to social media platforms like LinkedIn or Facebook.

If your sales or marketing depends on various social channels or a wide range of third-party tools, having to rig your own workarounds can bog down your efficiency, compared to software with built-in social sync that already does this.

### **Customization learning curve**

While you can customize a lot using Apptivo, the process can be challenging. Combined with the outdated UI, some users report complexity. Setting up workflows, custom fields, or new modules often means having to dive deeper into manuals or investing in a full support team.

Without someone technical on your side, getting a fully fine-tuned CRM system can drag on, wasting time and energy.

## Feature deep-dive ⚙️

So, what does Apptivo actually offer? Apptivo checks many boxes: management functionality, billing, workflow automation, and even a mobile app for work on the go.

Here’s a closer look at how the features come together.

### **Contact and lead management** 👤

Strong lead management starts with clean data, and Apptivo does a good job here. Every app supports custom fields, so you can capture details that are necessary to your sales cycle, whether it’s budget ranges, product interests, or industry tags. Leads and contacts flow through the system with ease through notifications and reminders for follow-ups, so you never miss an opportunity to connect (or reconnect).

Lead scoring isn’t out of the box, but you can mimic it by setting up workflow rules. For example, you might automatically bump priority when a lead requests a demo or opens several emails. Combined with built-in templates for email marketing and calls, you can make a structured sales process without needing outside tools.

Despite these great workarounds, they do bring a steeper learning curve for small businesses new to using CRM software.

### **Project management and time tracking** ⏱️

Apptivo’s project management capabilities are deeper than those of many small-business CRMs.

Here are some project and pipeline management tools to expect:

- **Interactive drag-and-drop Gantt chart**: Visualizes dependencies and schedules across tasks and sub-projects.
- **Built-in milestones**: Break projects into checkpoints and track progress stage by stage.
- **Time tracking:** Use timesheets or a stopwatch, which can be manager- or customer-approved for each project. You can then convert those logs straight to billing.
- **Templates:** Reuse across projects. Combine with milestones, set them once and launch the same blueprint over and over.

### **Invoicing and quoting** 📋

Billing is where some CRMs fall short. Apptivo handles it natively with the one-click QuickBooks sync. That means you can turn invoices and expense reports into journal entries and sync them with QuickBooks.

Just note that Accounts tied to products or sales in QuickBooks Online are only pulled under the Income, Expense, and Inventory Asset Account. If you’re new to QuickBooks Online, you’ll need to set up a new Account for products or sales directly in QuickBooks first.

### **Automation and workflows** 🦾

Manual admin tasks can eat up hours in a team’s week. Apptivo gives you automation capacity that scales with your plan, starting at 25 workflows on the Lite tier and up to 300 workflows on Enterprise.

These can handle repetitive tasks like sending a welcome email after a form submission, creating a follow-up task after a meeting, or moving deals through pipeline management stages.

It doesn’t reach the level of full marketing automation, but it’s powerful enough for a CRM-focused tool. That said, the number of allowed workflows (number of triggers) can still feel limiting, especially on lower tiers, while some alternatives offer far more flexibility, or even unlimited automations per account.

### **Mobile app experience** 📱

The mobile app is an important extension of any cloud-based platform. Available on iOS and Android, the Apptivo mobile app covers the essentials, with 20 out of 30 of its features being available, like updating contacts, creating tasks, logging time, sending invoices, and checking project progress. For small teams on the move, it keeps key data within reach.

## Pricing breakdown: What you really pay 💵

On the surface, Apptivo looks affordable compared to other CRM platforms. The real cost, however, depends on which tier you choose and the add-ons you’ll likely need.

Here’s a clear overview of how Lite, Premium, Ultimate, and Enterprise paid Apptivo plans stack up:

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Feature** | **Lite** | **Premium** | **Ultimate** | **Enterprise** |
| Pricing | $15 per user/month (billed annually) | $25 per user/month (billed annually) | $40 per user/month (billed annually) | Custom pricing |
| Core CRM features (contacts, leads, opportunities) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

There are some hidden costs to watch out for when choosing Apptivo:

- **Paid training**: $125/hr for onboarding, extra setup, or training new hires.
- **Advanced automation**: Only available with Ultimate or Enterprise.
- **Email campaigns**: Start at $10 for 5,000 emails. Costs climb fast if you run campaigns regularly. Purchased emails never expire, but frequent sends will rack up fees.

In comparison, many of the features that competitors include in mid-tier are still locked behind Ultimate or Enterprise for Apptivo. Plus, you’ll need to budget for add-ons.

If you’re already using other Zoho products, Zoho CRM makes more sense since its lower tiers already include broader automation and integrations than Apptivo’s Lite or Premium.

For businesses that run heavily on QuickBooks, Method CRM lets you [do more with your QuickBooks data](https://www.method.me/blog/do-more-with-your-quickbooks-data/) via its real-time, two-way QuickBooks sync, built-in workflow automations, and API access, even at the entry level.

Meanwhile, HubSpot CRM appeals to smaller teams with its forever-free plan for up to three users.

Apptivo’s value ultimately depends on whether the appeal of its bundled apps is enough to make up for the essentials being locked behind the higher tiers.

## Frequently asked questions

## Does Apptivo offer a forever-free plan?

Yes. Apptivo’s Standard plan is free forever for up to three users. The plan lets you use some of the apps available on the paid plans, has email and phone support, and stores up to 500 MB of documents. You only upgrade when you need more features.

What do you like best about Apptivo?

Honestly, what I like best about Apptivo is how it’s this huge all‑in‑one suite that we can tweak to fit our distribution workflow, instead of forcing us to adapt our process to the software. I’m Supply Chain Operations Manager at Northwood Distribution Partners, we’re 201–500 people, with warehouse teams, purchasing coordinators, sales, and finance all touching different parts of our order and supplier pipeline. Before testing Apptivo, we were juggling separate CRM, purchase order tools, a basic inventory tracker, and a separate help desk for supplier questions. It was messy, and data never lined up cleanly between systems.

The customizability is the real winner for us. We don’t just use it out of the box. I added custom fields to the supplier record pages to log lead time variances, carrier preferences, and quality issue history for each vendor. Our warehouse team needed custom views that only show open pick lists and backordered SKUs, while our purchasing staff sees reorder thresholds and pending PO approvals. We built a simple automation that fires off an internal Slack alert whenever stock drops below our safety level for fast‑moving pallet items. Last quarter, we had a critical component supplier delay hit us hard because our old system didn’t flag low inventory fast enough. With this setup now, our buyers get notified right away, and they can jump straight into the supplier profile, pull past delivery notes, and fire off a follow‑up email without switching tabs.

I also love that the CRM, purchasing, inventory, and invoicing modules talk to each other natively. When our sales team logs a new customer order, it feeds straight into the inventory app. If we don’t have enough stock, it auto‑generates a draft PO for our purchasing team to review and send to the supplier. Once that PO gets marked received, inventory levels update automatically, and finance can pull that receipt over to create the supplier invoice. We used to manually copy order numbers and quantities across three different platforms, and it created tons of typos. One example I still remember: we duplicated a large PO for packaging stock earlier this year because someone retyped the order number wrong. That mistake tied up warehouse space and cash for weeks. That kind of human error is way less likely now with the connected workflow inside Apptivo.

Another big plus is the mobile access for our floor staff. Our forklift operators and receiving team aren’t sitting at desks all day. They can pull up the receiving log, mark items as received, add notes about damaged pallets, and attach photos directly from their phones. Those notes attach right to the corresponding PO and supplier record. Before, they’d scribble damage notes on paper, hand them to an admin at the end of the shift, and half the context would get lost before it reached purchasing. Now we have a clear audit trail for every shipment, which helps us negotiate claims and hold unreliable suppliers accountable.

It’s also helpful for our software evaluation process, since I test a lot of SaaS stacks for the company. Apptivo lets us turn modules on and off gradually. We rolled out the PO and supplier apps first, waited a month, then brought in the customer CRM and help desk for supplier support tickets. We didn’t have to force the whole team to learn everything at once. Training was way smoother.

It’s not perfect, but the fact that one platform covers so many of our supply chain touchpoints, and we can reshape it to match how our distribution operation actually runs, saves our team hours of redundant data entry every single week. To be straightforward, Apptivo has some pretty frustrating downsides that have popped up as we’ve rolled it out across our distribution team at Northwood Distribution Partners. First off, the UI feels clunky and inconsistent between modules. The CRM page layout doesn’t match the purchase order screen, and the inventory module has its own separate menu structure. It sounds small, but it creates constant confusion. We trained our purchasing team on the PO workflow, and then when they need to hop into inventory to check stock levels, they’re lost all over again. Just last week, one of our buyers spent 20 minutes hunting for the supplier lead time field because it lives in a completely different spot than the matching notes section on POs. Our warehouse crew, who use mobile view most of the time, get hit even harder. The mobile interface is cramped, and some custom fields we built on the desktop version don’t render properly on their phones. Receiving staff have accidentally submitted incomplete receiving logs a couple times because a required damage note box was hidden off-screen.

Then there’s the reporting builder. It’s powerful once you figure it out, but the learning curve is brutal. We need regular reports: open backorders, supplier on-time delivery rates, inventory turnover by SKU, POs pending approval. I’m comfortable digging into SaaS tools, but our finance coordinator struggles constantly. The filter logic is counterintuitive, and there’s no simple way to save shared report templates that update cleanly for different users. If I build an on-time delivery report for our purchasing lead, they can’t easily tweak it to only show their own vendor list without breaking the whole thing. We’ve had a few instances where someone ran a report and pulled incorrect data because they mixed up date range filters, which almost messed up our weekly supplier performance review.

Permission management is another weak spot. The role settings are broad and don’t give us fine control we really need for supply chain. We want our receiving team to mark shipments as received and add damage photos, but we don’t want them able to edit PO pricing or supplier payment terms. Right now, the permissions bundle too many actions together. If you grant access to update receiving logs, that same user can accidentally modify cost data. We had a close call a month back; a warehouse lead updated a received quantity and inadvertently overwrote the unit cost on a packaging PO. It took finance hours to track down and correct that error before it hit our accounts payable. We end up being overly restrictive with warehouse accounts as a workaround, which slows them down when they need to make quick updates. Review collected by and hosted on G2.com.

What problems is Apptivo solving and how is that benefiting you?

For our distribution business at Northwood Distribution Partners, Apptivo is mainly fixing the huge disconnect we had between sales, purchasing, warehouse, and finance. Before we started testing it, every department was relying on its own siloed toolset. Our sales team used a standalone CRM to log customer orders, purchasing tracked suppliers and POs in a separate spreadsheet system, warehouse staff updated inventory on a basic tracking app, and finance pulled all that information manually to create invoices and reconcile payments. Data had to be retyped or copied over constantly, and it was so easy for numbers to fall out of sync. We’d run into mismatched order quantities, outdated stock counts, and missing supplier notes all the time.

The biggest problem it solves is eliminating that duplicate data entry. When a sales rep enters a new customer order in the Apptivo CRM, that order flows directly into the inventory module. If we don’t have enough stock to fulfill it, the system can kick off a draft purchase order for our buyers to review and send out to suppliers. Once our receiving team marks that shipment as received on their mobile device, inventory levels update automatically, and finance can pull that PO receipt to generate the supplier invoice. That whole chain used to require three or four separate manual handoffs. We’ve cut out so much copy-paste work, and the risk of typos or duplicated POs is way lower than before.

It also gives us one single, shared source of truth for every supplier record. Previously, supplier lead times, quality complaints, delivery delays, and claim documentation were scattered across emails, shared drive folders, and individual spreadsheets. Now we store all of that inside the supplier profile in Apptivo. Our buyers can quickly pull up a vendor’s full performance history before placing a new order. When the warehouse uploads photos of damaged pallets during receiving, those attachments tie straight to the corresponding PO and supplier file. That audit trail makes it much easier for us to follow up on freight claims and hold inconsistent suppliers accountable.

Another pain point it addresses is our lack of consistent visibility for low stock and backorders. We built simple automations that send internal alerts to purchasing whenever stock for high-volume SKUs drops below our safety threshold.
